key_insight: Materials behavior is modeled as a probabilistic ensemble of competing mechanisms, where emergent outcomes arise from which mechanisms activate, interact, and evolve under changing conditions.
engineering_relevance: This framework can improve prediction and design of fatigue damage tolerance by turning crack growth and arrest into an inference problem over competing unit processes.
method: Represent behavior as an ensemble of constituent mechanisms across scales
Connect mechanism activation, state evolution, and macroscopic observables probabilistically
Use the framework to integrate simulation, characterization, and machine learning
evidence_signal: The abstract presents a perspective framework and motivates it with fatigue crack propagation as a case study, but does not report quantitative results or benchmark performance.
watch_item: Practical use will depend on whether mechanism probabilities can be estimated reliably from sparse, noisy multiscale data.
paper_title: Materials Behavior as Mechanism Ensembles: A Probabilistic Framework for Emergent Behaviors
